title: P0 · Before the season — keys and codes are shared
description: Onesa's HIE publishes the public keys it signs health documents with to the WHO GDHCN trust network, and shares the national code systems its IPS uses with the WHO Terminology Service. Nothing about Kamal yet: this is what lets a Taifafeki clinic trust and read an Onesan record months later. Step A of the overview of key process flows.

steps.title: Keys and codes are shared
steps.headline: Before anyone travels, Onesa's signing keys and code systems reach the trust network, so a Taifafeki clinic can trust and read an Onesan record months later.
steps.narrative: Onesa's HIE publishes the public keys it signs health documents with to the WHO GDHCN trust network, and shares the national code systems its IPS uses with the WHO Terminology Service. Nothing about Kamal yet: this is what lets a Taifafeki clinic trust and read an Onesan record months later. Step A of the overview of key process flows.

experiences.doing: Publishes the public keys it signs health documents with to GDHCN, and shares its national code systems with the WHO Terminology Service.
Lists Onesa's keys alongside those of every other participant, including Taifafeki.

steps.painPoint: Without published keys, a Taifafeki clinic has no way to tell a genuine Onesan record from a forged one.
steps.enabler: Both countries take part in one trust network, so each trusts the other's keys without a bilateral agreement.
steps.policy: Which Onesan institution signs health documents on behalf of the health sector, and who in Taifafeki decides to accept that signature?

handoff.summary: Onesa's keys and code systems are known to the trust network
handoff.payload: Public signing keys (DSCs); national code systems

gaps: No business process or transaction for publishing keys or terminologies.
